items.title: Player minutes are only known for 50 of 465 players
items.detail: The official Players Traditional table publishes 465 rows across 10 pages; only page 1 (the 50 highest scorers) is present in the page source available to a plain fetch. Minutes for the other 415 players were left blank, not estimated. Two consequences: (a) the availability impact on the Injuries page is a measured LOWER BOUND and is 0.00 for several teams whose injured players fall outside the top 50; (b) player-prop coverage is limited to those 50 players.

items.title: No official-book price exists, so 'the line we bet against' is a model, not a market
items.detail: No sportsbook price is published by an NBA-operated source, so no official link can be attached to one. The site therefore bets the originated line against a deliberately naive REFERENCE line built from the same official ratings. A 'win' here means the model beat the naive model, not that it beat a book. Real expected value cannot be stated untilmarket prices are logged.

items.suggested_action: Log closing prices from a licensed odds source into data/raw/market.json with a per-row source field. Until then, read 'units' as model-vs-naive-model units.

items.title: Five modelling constants are choices, not official measurements
items.detail: Shrinkage constant k, the offense/defence split of an availability loss (alpha = 0.60), the availability impact coefficient (15.0 net-rating points per 100 possessions at 100% minutes lost), the status weights (Out 1.00 / Doubtful 0.70 / Questionable 0.35 / Probable 0.10), and the three player-prop multipliers are all modelling choices. k is now derived by an empirical-Bayes reliability calculation, but the single-game noise term in that calculation is estimated on the test window, so k is partly test-informed. A fixed-k sensitivity sweep is published on the Validation page.

items.title: Parlay and same-game-parlay correlations are model-derived, not measured

The side/total value of 0.00 is a mathematical property of the additive model under equal team-score variances; the player-market values are estimates.

items.title: Every strategy is still short of the 30-play sample gate
items.detail: The out-of-sample window is now 51 games (2026-11-06 to 2026-11-12), all of them predicted from ratings computed on 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05. The best-graded strategy, S1, has 23 graded plays at 16-7 (+7.55 model units, 32.8% ROI at -110). Its exact binomial p-value is 0.093 and the Wilson 95% interval on its hit rate is [0.491, 0.844] - the lower bound sits below the 0.5238 break-even, so the skill gate fails. Every other strategy has fewer graded plays. The residual standard deviation of the game margin is 17.4 points, so a swing of three or four games is well inside chance.

items.title: GitHub Pages is not publishing at all: the site's source is the legacy builder, which fails on every commit, so the live site is frozen at 2026-11-15T23:44Z
items.detail: Three explanations were recorded for this outage in order, and the first two were wrong. (1) Concurrency keys - the cause of the cancelled era, already fixed before this cycle. (2) Runner-pool starvation - measured and real (33 queued runs; two probe runs in progress for over an hour), but it explains the queueing, not the failures. (3) The actual cause, measured independently by two sessions: `GET /repos/.../pages` returns `build_type: legacy` with source `main:/`, and under the legacy builder `actions/deploy-pages` cannot publish while the legacy Jekyll build returns `Page build failed.` for every commit. Every `pages build and deployment` run since afc79f2 (2026-11-15T23:44Z, the last success) is `errored` with exactly that message, including for 1f962e2 and 37a3be3. Content causes were ruled out by measurement rather than assumption: 18 MB across 720 tracked files, largest 1.28 MB, no symlinks, no non-ASCII or reserved filenames, `.nojekyll` present and tracked, no `_config.yml` and no `Gemfile`. The live landing page read on 2026-11-16T03:05Z still shows the 23:44Z content (34 games in the 15-18 Nov horizon, 87 open flags), which is that build, not main. `PUT /repos/.../pages {build_type: workflow}` returns HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration', so no session token can fix it.
items.affected: every published page: the live site is frozen at afc79f2 (2026-11-15T23:44Z) and shows none of the 11/16 work - not the settlement page, not the player logs, not flags F92-F106
items.suggested_action: Repository owner action, one setting: Settings -> Pages -> Build and deployment -> Source: GitHub Actions. Until that is switched, no merge by any session can reach the live site and no deploy check can pass. Independently, the probe workflow should stay off the push trigger (already done in CI this cycle) so the queue does not re-congest afterwards.

items.title: The market anchor earns no detectable weight, so the published blend is 100% model
items.detail: scripts/market_anchor.py fits the blending weight w on 60 out-of-sample games (2026-11-06..11-13) whose pre-tip model and reference probabilities both exist in docs/data/backtest.json. Two proper rules were used. Log-loss picks w = 0.6449, but the 2,000-rep bootstrap 95% CI is [0.0000, 1.0000] - the whole admissible range - and the improvement over the pure model is 0.00672 with one-sided p = 0.313. Brier picks a different weight, w = 0.6330, so the two proper rules do not rank linear blends identically; an earlier reading of this repository that said they always do has been withdrawn in the output file. With a CI like that, publishing any non-zero weight would be a choice rather than a measurement, so the applied weight is 0 and the site says so.

items.suggested_action: Do not raise the weight until the CI excludes zero. The reason the interval is this wide is sample size: 60 games cannot resolve a 0.007 log-loss difference. Re-fit as the corpus grows and only promote w when the lower bound clears 0.

items.title: The pinned home-court advantage is computed on a stale standings read, and the published file contains two different standings-derived samples
items.detail: The HCA the model is pinned to is 1.23 points, from a measured home-win rate of 0.5285 on 193 games. That figure was measured from the official standings at the 2026-11-16T02:12Z..02:17Z capture, and it was honestly labelled as including only the 11/15 games that had gone Final at that moment. All three games that finished afterwards (HOU@WAS, ATL@MIL, OKC@SAC) were AWAY wins, so re-adding the official standings at 14:3xZ in this session gives home W-L 102-94 = 196 games, a home-win rate of 0.5204, and a pinned HCA of 0.88 points rather than 1.23. The drift reconciles EXACTLY: +3 games, +0 home wins, +3 road wins, which is precisely those three away wins - verified by verify/2026-11-16-23b323a3/verify_hca_anchor.py, which also re-checks the two internal consistency identities on the live table (home wins 102 == road losses 102; road wins 94 == home losses 94). A second, separate problem is visible in the same JSON: data/derived/horizon_lines_v2.json meta.home_court_anchor reports measured_home_win_rate 0.5285 with games_measured 161, while its own standings_cross_check sub-object reports 0.5285 over 193 games and the final-score corpus measures 0.5155 over 161. The rate and the game count in the top-level fields do not come from the same sample.

So the deploy backlog is not only a concurrency-key problem: the account's runner pool is being consumed by ~1-hour probe runs plus one refresh/publish pair per push per branch, and nothing in this repository bounds the number of branches pushing. The group keys are now correct (probe-official globally; pages-deploy serialised and never cancelled), which stops deploys from being killed, but it cannot create runners.
